messages:
Chris: Opening the open Q&A thread from today's all-hands — ask leadership anything about who we're trying to win for, our mission, positioning, competitors.
Jules: Quick clarifying Q — are we doubling down on "developer-first" or broadening to platform buyers? wondering about signal to enterprise sales.
Maya: Developer-first still core. We optimize the onboarding + API experience, but product features (SLA, VPC, quota) are tuned to make it saleable to platform teams. It's a two-stage go-to-market.
Devon: From field: enterprises ask if we run their models or if we host only. short answer?
Chris: We don't aim to own the model layer. Our moat is serving: latency/cost/reliability + observability. We'll partner for model support but not compete on model IP.
Lina: How do we express that in docs? want a one-liner for sales decks.
Maya: Proposed: "We make LLMs practical in production — predictable latency, unit economics, and rollout controls across hosted, dedicated, and private." Thoughts?
Jules: sounds good. Add "developer-first" at front maybe: "Developer-first platform..."
Ivy: Competitors ask: how are we different from managed endpoints (cloud) vs API-first LLM vendors? short bullets please.
Chris: short bullets: 1) unified runtime across environments, 2) cost-aware controls (batching/caching/quantization), 3) production-grade observability and rollout tooling, 4) SLA-backed dedicated capacity. That's our narrative.
Devon: pricing ask: how flexible on committed vs usage? customers want blends.
Chris: We offer usage-based hosted API + reserved capacity for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing for Private. Blends via committed burst/overage options.
Lina: technical: when we say "unified runtime" — is it the same binary in private and hosted? any feature divergence expected?
Maya: same core runtime, but private may ship with additional infra glue (KMS, audit sinks). We keep feature parity in APIs.
Jules: For selling to regulated customers — what are the must-have checklist items? (quick list)
Maya: VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, on-prem option, SOC/ISO artifacts.
Devon: objection: do customers care about kernel-level optimizations? how to communicate without getting too nerdy.
Lina: show outcomes: e.g., "X% lower token cost" and latency numbers vs common baselines. include sample config snippet in docs.
Maya: snippet for rollout policy:
```json
{"canary": true, "routes": ["hosted","dedicated"], "fallback": "quantized-small"}
```
Jules: Any comment on expansion: do we expect to build horizontal developer tools or verticals (search, agents, retrieval)?
Chris: Platform-first horizontally but we'll fund vertical templates and examples. We want repeatable customer patterns via templates but not heavy verticalized products at launch.
Ivy: last question — what is the 12mo metric that determines success?
Chris: Adoption + value: 1) growth in paid endpoints, 2) percentage of traffic on Dedicated, 3) SLO attainment + cost-per-token improvements. If those trend positive, we doubled down.
Devon: thanks — will use this to prep next deck. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Deployed all-hands replay link: https://videos.redwood.ai/ah/3301112222 :white_check_mark:
Chris: thanks all — keep the Qs coming, we'll summarize and add to product FAQ. :sparkles:
